PresentationTitle: 2 - Project Scoping and App Platform Selection
Topic: Defining Project Scope in HCI Design, Overview of Target Application Platforms, Android Platform: Characteristics and Constraints, iOS Platform: Characteristics and Constraints, Windows Platform: Characteristics and Constraints, Web Platform: Characteristics and Constraints, Platform Selection: Criteria and Decision-Making, Design and Development Tools by Platform

Slides.Title: 2 - Project Scoping and App Platform Selection
Bullets: Establishing clear project boundaries, platform choices, and tool selections before design begins.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: Welcome to this module on project scoping and platform selection. Before any design work begins, teams must define what they are building, who they are building it for, and what tools and platforms they will use. This presentation walks through each of those decisions systematically.

Slides.Title: Defining Project Scope in HCI Design
Bullets: Project scope sets boundaries on what will and will not be addressed.
Goals articulate intended outcomes and guide all design decisions.
Constraints include time, budget, technology, and team expertise.
Target audience shapes platform, features, and design style.
A formal project description documents all scoping decisions.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: Project scope is the foundation of any HCI design effort. Without clearly defined scope, projects risk creep, misaligned expectations, and wasted effort. Goals tell the team where they are headed. Constraints define what is realistic. Understanding the target user audience is one of the most consequential early decisions — it directly influences platform choice, feature prioritization, and interaction style. The formal project description brings all of these elements together into a single authoritative reference document that the team can consult throughout the project lifecycle.

Slides.Title: Overview of Target Application Platforms
Bullets: Four primary platforms: Android, iOS, Windows, and Web.
Additional platforms include wearables, voice assistants, and smart TVs.
Mobile, desktop, and web represent distinct user contexts.
Each category has unique interaction models and technical environments.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: This course focuses on four main platforms: Android mobile, iOS mobile, Windows desktop, and web-based applications. Each has its own design paradigms, toolchains, and user expectations. Beyond these four, designers should be aware that interactive applications also run on wearables, voice assistants, smart TVs, and embedded systems — these platforms are increasingly relevant in the broader HCI field. The three broad categories — mobile, desktop, and web — each represent meaningfully different contexts of use, which influences nearly every design decision.

Slides.Title: Android and iOS: Mobile Platform Characteristics
Bullets: Android is open-source, running on many manufacturers' devices.
Material Design guides Android UI with tactile, adaptive layouts.
Device fragmentation and permissions are key Android constraints.
iOS offers tight hardware-software integration on Apple devices.
Apple's Human Interface Guidelines emphasize clarity and depth.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: Android, developed by Google, runs on an enormous variety of devices, which introduces significant fragmentation challenges — designers cannot assume consistent screen sizes, hardware capabilities, or OS versions. Material Design provides a unifying visual and interaction language. iOS, by contrast, runs exclusively on Apple hardware, enabling a more consistent design target. Apple's Human Interface Guidelines emphasize clarity, deference to content, and a sense of depth through layering and translucency. iOS distribution is tightly controlled through the App Store, which enforces quality standards but also introduces review and approval constraints for developers and designers.

Slides.Title: Windows and Web: Desktop and Browser Platforms
Bullets: Windows dominates desktop computing for productivity and enterprise use.
Fluent Design System guides Windows apps with light, depth, and motion.
Hardware diversity and legacy OS versions are Windows constraints.
Web apps run in browsers without installation, maximizing accessibility.
Responsive design and WCAG standards guide web application design.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: Windows supports complex, feature-rich applications designed for mouse, keyboard, and large-screen environments. Microsoft's Fluent Design System provides a coherent visual language emphasizing light, depth, motion, material, and scale. Designers must account for a wide range of hardware configurations and the reality that many enterprise users run older OS versions. The web platform is unique in its universal reach — any device with a browser can access a web application. Web design is guided by established usability conventions, WCAG accessibility standards, and responsive design principles rather than a single vendor's design system. Web apps face constraints around browser compatibility, network dependency, and the limitations of web APIs compared to native platform APIs.

Slides.Title: Platform Selection: Criteria and Decision-Making
Bullets: Match the platform to where target users actually are.
Required features must align with platform capabilities and APIs.
Team skills and tool availability should factor into the decision.
Document and justify the platform choice in the project description.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: Selecting the right platform is a structured decision, not a guess. The most important driver is the target user audience — designers should choose the platform their users already use and prefer. Next, the project's required features must be achievable on that platform; hardware access, performance requirements, and available APIs all matter. Within an academic context, team skills and tool availability are also legitimate and practical factors. Whatever the rationale, the platform selection decision must be explicitly documented in the formal project description, including the reasoning behind it so that reviewers and stakeholders can evaluate the choice.

Slides.Title: Design and Prototyping Tools
Bullets: Wireframing and prototyping precede development on all platforms.
Figma is widely used for wireframes, mockups, and interactive prototypes.
Adobe XD and Sketch are additional professional prototyping options.
Prototypes allow testing and iteration before committing to code.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: Regardless of which platform a team targets, the HCI design process typically begins with low- and high-fidelity prototyping tools. Figma has become the industry standard for collaborative design and prototyping, supporting real-time collaboration and interactive prototype testing. Adobe XD and Sketch are also widely used in professional contexts. The key value of these tools is that they allow designers to explore ideas, gather feedback, and iterate rapidly without writing production code, reducing the cost of design changes significantly.

Slides.Title: Platform-Specific Development Tools
Bullets: Android: Android Studio IDE with Kotlin as the recommended language.
iOS: Xcode IDE with Swift; requires a macOS computer.
Windows: Visual Studio with C#, WinUI 3, and .NET frameworks.
Web: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript form the foundational tech stack.
Web tools include VS Code and browser-based development environments.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: Each platform has a canonical development toolchain. Android development centers on Android Studio, Google's official IDE, with Kotlin as the recommended language. iOS development requires Xcode and Swift, and critically, it requires a macOS computer — a real constraint for teams without Apple hardware. Windows application development is done primarily in Visual Studio using C#, WinUI 3, and the .NET ecosystem. Web development is the most accessible entry point, with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as the foundational stack, and Visual Studio Code as a widely adopted, free, cross-platform editor.

Slides.Title: Cross-Platform Tools and Frameworks
Bullets: Cross-platform frameworks target multiple platforms from one codebase.
React Native, Flutter, and .NET MAUI are leading frameworks.
Advantages include reduced development time and shared logic.
Trade-offs include reduced native experience quality and performance.
Framework choice should align with team skills and project goals.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: Cross-platform frameworks are an increasingly popular choice, especially for teams with limited resources. React Native, Flutter, and .NET MAUI each allow a single codebase to deploy to Android, iOS, and in some cases web or desktop. The primary advantage is development efficiency — write once, deploy many times. However, there are real trade-offs: cross-platform apps may not fully conform to each platform's design conventions, can face performance limitations compared to fully native apps, and sometimes lag behind when new platform features are released. Teams should weigh these trade-offs carefully in the context of their specific project goals and skill sets.

Slides.Title: Summary: Scoping and Platform Selection
Bullets: Define scope early: goals, constraints, audience, and platform.
Know the four primary platforms and their distinct design systems.
Match platform selection to users, features, and team capability.
Select appropriate tools for prototyping and development.
Document all decisions in the formal project description.
Slides.SpeakerNotes: To summarize: effective HCI project work begins with rigorous scoping — defining what you are building, for whom, under what constraints, and on which platform. The four primary platforms — Android, iOS, Windows, and Web — each have distinct design conventions, development tools, and constraints. Platform selection should be driven by the target audience, feature requirements, and team capability, and the rationale must be formally documented. Prototyping tools like Figma support early design work across all platforms, while platform-specific IDEs and frameworks support development. All of these decisions belong in the formal project description, which serves as the team's authoritative reference throughout the project.
